title: Unconditional full-B2 bound (coefficient 31/10, exponent 1) for one fixed uniform NP family, with explicit disperser dimension and explicit o(n) remainder

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"One fixed total family f_n:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, defined uniformly for every integer n>=1 with no advice and no per-length choice, as the Ben-Sasson-Kopparty construction with p=2 (Theorem 2.2 of 'Affine Dispersers from Subspace Polynomials', preprint of 2010-03-12, journal version SIAM J. Comput. 41(4):880-914, 2012), instantiated exactly as fixed in proof.md Section 2 and disperser.md: f_0(empty)=0; for n>=1 let k be the least prime with k>2*n^(3/5), r=ceil(n/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)); let q_k be the monic irreducible polynomial of degree k over F_2 returned by the fixed deterministic Shoup algorithm, K=F_2[Z]/(q_k) with F_2-basis 1,Z,...,Z^(k-1); let phi:F_2^n->K^r be the injective F_2-linear map that splits x into consecutive k-bit blocks (last block zero-padded) and reads each block in that basis, and let pi:K->F_2 be the constant-coefficient functional (nontrivial, pi(1)=1); put y_i=phi_i(x)^(2^(i+1)-1) for i=1..r and f_n(x)=pi(Sym_r^t(y_1,...,y_r)), where Sym_r^t is the t-th elementary symmetric polynomial. Every object in this definition is a deterministic function of n alone.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"10","numerator":"31"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"10","numerator":"31"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total family, which one fixed polynomial-time evaluator computes at every length and which is therefore in NP with the empty witness (witness bound zero, both directions proved), the following hold in the full Li-Yang B2 model, i.e. deterministic acyclic one-output circuits with two input pins per gate over all 16 binary truth tables, unbounded depth and fan-out, exact computation on every input, each retained gate counted once and inputs, wires and output selection costing nothing: every B2 circuit C computing f_n satisfies |C| >= (31/10)*n - (261/10)*d(n) - 128/5, where d(n)=floor(6*n^(4/5))+1 is the affine-disperser dimension of f_n, and d(n)/n tends to 0. Hence for every real epsilon>0 there is an integer N_epsilon such that for EVERY integer n>=N_epsilon, C_B2(f_n) >= (31/10-epsilon)*n. Therefore liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/n >= 31/10, so the declared pair is exactly (coefficient, exponent) = (31/10, 1). Nothing stronger is asserted: no coefficient above 31/10, no exponent above 1, no logarithmic factor and no lane or global endpoint is claimed anywhere in this submission.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: Unscored lemma A (no score requested; strictly weaker than, and about a different family than, the main theorem). Let g_n:{0,1}^n->{0,1} be OR, with g_0(empty)=0, and L'={x in {0,1}^*: some bit of x is 1}, so x in L' iff g_|x|(x)=1 and the empty string is not in L'. L' is in P, hence in NP, with the empty-witness verifier V(x,w)=1 iff w is empty and g_|x|(x)=1, witness bound W=0. Then C_B2(g_n)=n-1 for every n>=2: the binary OR tree gives <=n-1, and for the lower bound trimming to the ancestors of the output leaves a connected graph on n inputs, g gates and k constant nodes needing at least n+g+k-1 distinct edges while the 2g input pins supply at most 2g, so g>=n-1+k>=n-1. Hence liminf C_B2(g_n)/n = 1 and the pair (1,1) is valid for this family, while (2,1) is false by the OR-tree upper bound. Complete proof in proof.md Section 7 and lp-arithmetic.md Section 5. This lemma supplies neither coordinate of the main claim and no endpoint.

Unscored lemma B (no score requested; finite rational arithmetic only, not a circuit theorem). For the unchanged Li-Yang Theorem 4.1 linear program on the admissible region alpha_I,alpha_Q,alpha_phi>=0, 0<=alpha_phi<=1/2, 0<=alpha_Q<=alpha_I, with u=delta-alpha_I and u bounded by each of the six terms alpha_I/3, 2-2alpha_phi+alpha_Q, 4-4alpha_phi, 3+alpha_phi, 5-alpha_Q and (5-2alpha_phi+alpha_Q)/2, the exact maximum of c=delta-alpha_I-alpha_phi/2 is 31/10. It is attained at (alpha_I,alpha_Q,alpha_phi,delta)=(48/5,9/5,1/5,64/5) where all six right-hand sides equal 16/5, and the matching upper certificate is (7/10)(3+alpha_phi)+(1/10)(5-alpha_Q)+(1/5)((5-2alpha_phi+alpha_Q)/2)=31/10+alpha_phi/2, so c<=31/10 throughout. Complete proof with exact fractions, and the computed lp-certificate output, in lp-arithmetic.md Sections 2, 3 and 6. This certifies arithmetic for the unchanged LP only; it awards no circuit coefficient, is not a barrier, and asserts nothing about other techniques.
